title: Compliance event subscription and evidence ingest API
creator: Priya Desai
description: Build a cohesive event subscription and evidence ingest surface for compliance consumers. This ticket covers: (1) a subscription API allowing customers and internal services to register for residency-change, retention-policy, and audit-evidence events; (2) a signed evidence-ingest endpoint used by internal jobs and trusted partners to push packaged audit artifacts (logs, manifests, KMS-wrapped blobs); and (3) delivery semantics, retry behavior, and observability for compliance notifications. The goal is to provide durable, auditable delivery of events and evidence with clear signing, idempotency, and residency constraints so downstream compliance systems can automate retention enforcement and evidence storage without manual polling.
acceptance_criteria: Customers or internal services can create/update/delete event subscriptions via POST/PUT/DELETE /v1/compliance/subscriptions and receive a subscription_id.
Subscription payload supports filters: event_type (audit|retention|residency), project_id, model_version, region, and retention_window.
Evidence ingest endpoint POST /v1/compliance/evidence accepts multipart metadata + encrypted artifact (max 200MB) and returns evidence_id with storage_location (S3 path or GCS URL).
All outbound event deliveries include signature headers (X-RW-Signature) and a delivery-id for deduplication; recipients can verify signature using published jwks_uri.
Delivery retry policy implemented: exponential backoff with jitter up to 72 hours, and at-least-once semantics with idempotency key support.
Events and evidence are tagged with residency region; evidence storage honors tenant-residency override when configured and is logged to audit index.
API surfaced in Swagger/OpenAPI with schema v1; integration tests cover subscription lifecycle, evidence upload, and signed delivery verification.
Telemetry: per-subscription delivery success/failure, latency, and bytes transferred emitted to console dashboards; retention enforcement metrics exported to prometheus.
Security review completed and KMS integration validated for evidence encryption at rest and in-transit.
Documentation and sample consumers (Node + Go) added to examples repo and linked in console subscription UX.
Backward-compatible: existing compliance notifier consumers continue to receive events until migration window ends.
Privacy: no PII included in event payloads unless explicitly requested and consented; when included, payloads must be KMS-wrapped and logged to restricted audit index.
api_contract: GET /v1/compliance/subscriptions/{subscription_id} -> subscription object with filters and delivery_config

POST /v1/compliance/evidence -> multipart: metadata JSON (evidence_type, tenant_id, region, retention_until, keys: [kms_key_id]), file: artifact (encrypted). Response: {evidence_id, storage_location, tombstone_token}
POST /v1/compliance/deliveries/ack -> {delivery_id, subscription_id, status} (for recipients to ACK synchronous delivery receipts)
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>, X-RW-Idempotency-Key (optional), X-RW-Signature, X-RW-Timestamp
Errors: 4xx for validation, 401/403 for auth, 429 for rate limits, 5xx for transient server errors with Retry-After header
webhook_delivery_guarantees: At-least-once delivery semantics by default. Each delivery includes a delivery_id for deduplication by consumers.
Retry schedule: 1m, 5m, 20m, 1h, 3h, 12h, 24h, 48h, 72h (then mark subscription as degraded and alert ops).
Signature scheme: ed25519 for high performance; public keys exposed at /.well-known/jwks.json. Requests include X-RW-Signature and X-RW-Timestamp to prevent replay.
Backpressure: if recipient responds 429, honor Retry-After but impose per-subscription exponential backoff to avoid thundering herd.
Failure handling: persistent failures escalate to console notifications and a dead-letter queue; failed evidence uploads are retained for 90 days for reprocessing.
Delivery modes: push (HTTP webhook), pull (S3 presigned URLs via periodic batch export), and streaming (Kafka topic for internal consumers).
evidence_packaging: Evidence envelope schema v1: {evidence_id, evidence_type, generated_at, tenant_id, residency_region, manifest: [{path, sha256}], kms_wrapped_key_ids}
Preferred artifact formats: tar.gz for bundle exports, newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) for event logs, and compressed parquet for analytics exports.
Encryption: artifacts must be encrypted with tenant KMS key or Redwood KMS on behalf; service returns storage_location with KMS context for access logs.
Retention metadata: evidence records include retention_until and retention_policy_id to drive automated deletion workflows.
Bulk export: support for signed bulk export requests via POST /v1/compliance/exports which returns presigned archive URLs and an export_manifest.
Proof-of-ingest: each evidence upload yields a tombstone_token that can be used to prove data receipt during audits.
Size limits and streaming support documented: direct upload up to 200MB; larger uploads via resumable multipart (recommended for >200MB).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable subscription API and evidence ingest for internal compliance team + two pilot customers in us-west-2; monitor delivery and storage costs.
Phase 2 (beta): open to enterprise tenants with residency requirements; add console subscription UI and sample consumer SDKs.
Phase 3 (GA): enable for all tenants; deprecate legacy notify-orchestrator endpoints after 90-day migration window.
Migration notes: run dual-delivery for 30 days (legacy + new) during pilot migrations; provide a migration helper script to translate subscription filters.
Monitoring: create dashboard with per-subscription success rate, avg latency, total bytes, and open dead-letter count; add alerts for >5% failure over 15m.
risks_and_mitigations: High throughput could increase storage/costs: mitigation - sampling policy, size caps, and retention automation to minimize long-term storage.
Signature key compromise: mitigation - rotate signing keys monthly, support key revocation list, and require recipients to validate timestamps and nonces.
Residency violations if evidence stored in wrong region: mitigation - residency tag enforced at upload time and validated by pre-storage gating; automated periodic residency audits.
Duplicate deliveries causing downstream double-processing: mitigation - delivery_id + idempotency key and example consumer code showing dedup handling.
Regulatory/legal edge cases (gov data): mitigation - require advance enablement and manual review for air-gapped evidence transfer; integrate with Private deployment flow.
